policy_title: Bring academies and free schools into local authority control and reform private school status
stated: Move academies and free schools into local authority control, remove charitable status from private schools, and charge full VAT on private school fees, with an interim exemption for SEND children while public capacity is built.

source.quote: Elected Greens will: • Move academies and free schools into local authority control, removing charitable status from private schools and charging full VAT on fees. Private school places for children with special education needs will not be subject to VAT. This will be an interim measure while public-sector capacity is built.

bearing_set.reason: Both limbs directly shape school governance (academy/free-school structure), state school capacity and standards (as private-school pupils may migrate into the state sector), and the affordability and attainment landscape for children across sectors, making this a non-negligible verdict on education and opportunity.

VAT at 20% on private school fees materially increases the tax burden on the households paying those fees, reducing their disposable spending power by a concrete, costed amount (IFS/OBR analysis estimated ~£1.7bn revenue, implying that sum extracted from fee-paying families).

VAT on private fees and removal of charitable status generate significant new public revenue, materially improving the funded/borrowed balance; this is a concrete fiscal gain that moves the debt-sustainability indicator.

Private school fees are concentrated among higher-income households; taxing them redistributes fiscal burden up the income distribution, plausibly narrowing the gap — a directly assessable distributional effect (IFS-style incidence analysis applies).

membership_note: The four bearings are: O7 (direct education-quality and capacity effect), O11 (concrete tax-burden increase on fee-paying households), O12 (material public revenue gain), and O14 (redistributive incidence narrowing income gap). O9 was considered for democratic-accountability of LA control but the strict O9 scope (anti-discrimination, voting rights, due process) is not met by a governance restructuring. O15 cohesion effects are plausible but the mechanism cannot be pinned to a specific indicator at non-negligible confidence.
